title: Huge Potential, Huge Shortcomings
body:
I’m trying to be consistent at gym, and a large part of this process is keeping track of my journey. I’ve found it to be incredibly helpful to have a plan laid out, and this app has certainly made it intuitive to do so. 

My biggest gripe is just that as well. Often, the apple watch sync removes sets, and even entirely fails to track my workouts after completion; I can’t see them in history. It’s incredibly frustrating. It’s encouraging to see the numbers and history rack up automatically, but having to manually plug them in again is irritating.

I’m also annoyed at the paywall, which removes the most basic features such as graphs.

One more thing, I’d hope to see a way to add notes to custom workout exercises. In other words, I can add custom instructions.

All in all, it could be perfect, but it’s just not there.

title: After trying app after app, Strong is the one I keep coming back to.
body:
For context, I bought Strong Pro (Lifetime) back around 2020–2021 on Android. When I switched to iPhone, I completely forgot about it, so I was pleasantly surprised years later when I logged in and still had my lifetime purchase. Some of the features I mention may be part of Strong Pro, but this review is simply based on my experience.

Before settling on Strong, I tried Hevy, Lift, Strongify, RepCount, Setgraph, Liftin’, and GymBook. My goal was simple: I wanted an app that let me manage my workouts directly from my Apple Watch. I don’t follow rigid workout plans, I go into the gym with a general idea and decide what to do based on how I’m feeling that day.

That ended up being the biggest issue with most other apps. Many expect you to build routines ahead of time and don’t handle free-form workouts very well. Others had features I liked but always seemed to compromise somewhere else.

Strong does exactly what I was looking for.

I can start a workout from my Apple Watch and, if needed, switch over to my phone, but the best part is that I don’t have to. I can add exercises on the fly, log sets, reps, and weights, track personal records, see my total weight lifted, monitor heart rate, calories burned, and elapsed workout time, all from my wrist.

The app is intuitive, the Apple Watch experience is excellent, and everything feels well thought out. I’m still discovering features, but I honestly haven’t run into a single moment where I thought, “I really wish this app had…”

Highly recommended. If I lost my lifetime license today, I’d happily pay the current price for Strong Pro again. That’s how impressed I’ve been with it.

title: The workout app field is expanding rapidly and Strong is getting left behind.
body:
I’m quickly finding that there’s no perfect workout app. There’s always a these things are great or improvements over this app…but…and the “but” is the key because it comes down to which app is offering the trade offs you’re willing to live without? 

My frustration with Strong is we are still dealing with syncing issues between the Apple Watch and the iPhone. The whole purpose of starting and ending workouts on the Watch was supposed to be to minimize these issues yet I still find I’m having increasingly more issues with ghost workouts - workouts started and ended on Apple Watch but instead of syncing they go into workout purgatory only to show up after you log out and log back in. If this wasn’t as frequent as it occurs it may be something you could deal with occasionally but it’s not.

Secondly, when you create exercises, you’re unable to assign body parts to them after saving them initially. Even if you go to the exercise library and edit them there. Additionally there’s no way to add photos. I beta test a lot of workout apps and this is one place where people are smoking Strong. Here’s why this matters: Strong doesn’t have a lot of common gym exercises in the library. So when you create them that means they also won’t have images or instructions on how to do them. Meanwhile Strong is starting to feel very Windows XP in a Windows 11 world.  This is also seen in the charts and graphs which seem flat and dated versus many newer apps offer richer charts and data presentation.

Likewise, there’s no options for having Strong enforce progressive overload which is something you’re seeing in more and more apps where they automatically boost or recommend boosting your weight on your next workout. This is great for people starting out on their fitness journeys that aren’t as familiar with these kinds of things. Not everyone is dedicated enough to watch hours of YouTube videos to figure them out.

Update: I think the part of the bigger picture that Strong misses is that you’re providing a part of the picture of someone’s fitness journey. Thinks that should be easy to get to like exporting workout data are buried under paths that don’t make sense like you clearly have a dedicated history button and you literally show my workout so why when I say share workout is it only showing the template info instead of the actual workout data - to get to the workout data it’s buried way over under settings with an option to do a CSV. The issue is this is you entire workout history - I do weekly check ins as do most people who are tracking their fitness metrics so this is a royal pain in the butt and a lot of extra steps to cut what you need and big picture: when EVERYONE does this there’s no efficient way to get your data points that you need because it becomes very time consuming.

title: Opportunity for improvement
body:
I’ve been using the Strong app for about two months now. I really like the app, I was able to put together comprehensive daily workout plans. One of the things I did that could potentially be an add-on to the app. For each exercise, I had a note that identifies the body part and specific sub category of the muscle worked for each exercise.  example:

Triceps Extension 
Target: Triceps (Lateral, Medial, Long Head

Bent-Over Reverse Flye
Target: Shoulders Rrear Deltoids)

Hammer Curl (Dumbbell)
Target: Biceps (Brachialis)

Would be nice if this information was in the description. Perhaps at the top showing what the exercise targets and the exact part of the anatomy/muscle.

Would also be helpful if when looking up the section that has sub categories, instead of just arms, it broke down, triceps, biceps and which part of the bicep or tricep the exercise effects.

I noticed this when the person introduced me to your app had multiple exercises for arms that the short head, but nothing for the long head or brachialis. Because he had no idea. The app could easily navigate someone to selecting exercise exercises for a full workout.

Just my thoughts. Still love the ad and will keep using it and recommend recommended to others.

Or at least let users upload their own videos/photos/notes when adding a new workout. 

I also think whenever you use a template for a workout, if you change it during your active workout and then finish - there should be a 3rd option to "Save As New" that doesn't alter your original template but allows you to save what you created as a whole new template. They only currently allow you to either keep your original template or override your original template.

I’ve been using Strong for a few years, and it’s served me well. It’s helped me track my workouts, stay consistent, and keep myself honest so I could continue making progress.

That said, the app hasn’t evolved much over the years. The UI feels a bit stale, and there haven’t been many meaningful new features added. As a result, I’ve decided to move on to a different app that feels fresher and offers a social component that Strong currently lacks.

Strong is still a solid workout tracker, and I’m grateful for the role it played in my fitness journey, but it’s no longer the best fit for me.

title: Owned/used since 2017; just needs active Lock Screen timer + widget
body: Title says it all! Love the app. Just need to be able to have a widget that shows me how much time is left on my set if I close out of the app (or a timer on the camera island at the top of the screen), and an active monitor on the lock screen that counts down, rather than just a notification that my timer is done

title: Best Workout App Hands Down
body: I went through every workout app when I first started using smartphone workout apps. Loved the simplicity from the beginning and the ability to record everything I was focused on and they’ve only built on people’s feedback to make it better. Love looking back at the calendar and seeing all of the workouts I knocked out. Keep going.

title: Best strength training tracking app out there
body: It’s simple and intuitive and the Apple Watch interface is perfect for tracking my workouts in real time.   Health integration is great, and you can export your data if you want. So glad I found this app.

title: Great Workout Companion
body:
I use this every time I lift since it makes it easy to track sets, weights, and reps. The UI with the Apple Watch and rest timer is a big seller, especially when compared to similar apps. 

2 things on my wishlist for this app:
1. Interface/connection with Strava for wholistic tracking of activities
2. Muscle group use after workout with days for recovery for those groups
I love it

title: I watch app stopped syncing with phone.
body: Last update hosed the syncing between a watch and iPhone. Uninstalled and reinstalled the app on the watch and it won’t accept my account password. Buggy software.

title: Please Add Step Metric!
body:
I love this app. I started using the free version at the beginning of the year to track my workouts and I’ve been seeing so much progress. 

The app has almost everything I need, with the exception being that I would love a step metric that I can use for the stairmaster. It currently only allows miles or kms for cardio and the stairmaster at my gym only shows steps or floors climbed. 

I wouldn’t ding any points for this or anything. This is absolutely a 5 star app. Just a feature that I would be happy to see added!

title: I am loving it
body: It’s a beautiful thing, this workout app. Simple interface but yet it’s so rich in experience. Wide library of exercises, provision of custom exercises, body measurement recording option, etc.

title: Best weight-workout app I’ve used
body:
7/25 update - the latest update has really slowed the app down. The integration with Apple Watch is annoying and it now takes time for the app to “sync”. If you don’t notice the Watch app connection at the beginning of a workout, the workout timer won’t start. Still no ability to check all reps in a set with one click. It gets really old clicking 11 or 13 reps per set for every exercise when I’m doing 15 exercises with 11+ sets per workout.

Original review:
I used Fitness Point for a few years before I came across the “Strong” app. The wide ranging versatility of Strong is vastly superior to Fitness Point. 

The paid version of Strong has multiple worthwhile upgrades over the free base app. For me, the ability to create more than 3 personal workouts was a key factor in going with the paid app.

My one “wish” for this app that I think would be an improvement would be to see the total weight moved in a single workout prior to hitting “finish”. It would help me hit more goals. I know I can go back and edit but it’s sort of a pain in the middle of a workout. Otherwise, this is a powerful workout app with wide versatility that should appeal to the majority of plate heads and other gym rats like me.

title: Slow updates, buggy as ***
body:
I’ve been a strong user since ~2018. I like it, I really do.

However there are *so* many bugs I run into *every single workout*. And it is infuriating to see that instead of fixing these bugs or improving the existing flow, y’all instead push an update to add …widgets!? 

The Apple Watch <-> iPhone sync engine is *terrible*. There’s literally no way y’all don’t know about this cause I have issues with it every single workout. I’ll mark a set as done on my phone then my watch won’t see it so I do it there, then I go back to my phone and I’ve lost like 5 sets and have to re-enter them.

My patience is wearing so thin. I’ve even sent multiple emails to the developers, including one that was being nothing but positive and understanding. However it’s been 3+ months since then and I have seen no (noticeable) improvements and I’m honestly not convinced the developers even care about this stuff? 

I really want to keep using Strong but y’all are making it harder and harder for me to stay and not move to a competitor. And honestly the only reason I haven’t is cause there is overhead in switching. 

Surely y’all care about craft and details more than this.

title: Exercise Search Improved
body: The search logic really sucked before the update - you had to type the exercise exactly, keyword didn't work at all. I am so happy with the update, works much better now. I'll be keeping this as my main workout tracker. Thanks team!

title: GREAT!
body:
Amazing app! One thing though:

Many machines at different locations may vary in difficulty per labeled weight (different pulley configurations, grip, etc.)

Users should be able to create custom, on device instances of the slight different machines, and label them accordingly.

title: Great!… but…
body: I love this the simplicity and ease of using this app to track exercise progress. However, I desperately need the developer to make the template update screens understandable! What the heck do they mean???

title: Amazing free app to keep track
body: I have been using it for a while. This app is very user friendly and easy to use. There are no annoying ads or processes. I love it. It has your history and it allows u to preform the workout again, meaning that if you have a set workout routine you do not have to re-enter every exercise each time. It also has built in timer so thats very convenient.

title: Incredibly good
body: All features are implemented well.

title: Love the app, sync getting worse
body: I’ve been using this app for years and have loved it. Recently, the quality seems to be slipping, or sync’ing between the phone and watch has gotten more difficult over the years. I was on the TestFlight, and figured that was the issue, but it’s just as bad on the App Store version. Going to hang in there for a little while longer before switching. I hope they are able to fix sync so I don’t have to think about moving all my workouts to another platform.

title: Erases data
body: If you use the “live sync” feature to track a workout using both the phone app and Apple Watch, the app will regularly lose sets you have already saved. Super frustrating that the app cannot perform its basic functionality.

title: Worthless on watch
body:
I wouldn’t recommend anyone try using the watch app in tandem with the phone app, it never works. 

Yes, I have reset my stuff, multiple times. Consistently freezes and un-syncs. 

Don’t bother.

title: Perfect workout app
body: Why is this app so good and take up such little space because I have a 12 mini and I need space every other workout app I have tried take up too much space or require a subscription to use this is perfect for my needs!

title: Why so many dudes
body: All the renderings are men. Maybe a setting to fix that would be nice.

title: Was Great, Constant Sync Issues
body: Have been using the app for a year or two now. Was great between the watch and the phone could track and adjust on both at the same time. Now I’ve had 2 workouts in the last week that won’t sync back to the phone no matter what. And the rest timers get funky if you try and track on your phone after starting on watch. If fixed backed to a 5/5 app.

title: Good app. Poor sync.
body: I’ve used this app for years to track my workouts. Overall, it’s good when it comes to tracking workouts, but the sync feature between the app and Apple Watch can suck. Sometimes it syncs fine and other times they won’t sync unless you reset the app on both the phone and Apple Watch. This issue is persistent enough to where I experience it on a pretty regular basis. I wouldn’t be paying for this app until these sync issues are addressed.

title: Mediocre UI
body:
UI is mediocre. Only 3 free templates and a $99 lifetime license. Get a $1 notebook and a box of pens. Your iPhone already has a timer. 
App is free otherwise to see the prebuilt templates.

title: Constantly fails Sync
body: Had been solid for years but lately I can't get it to sync with the watch. What a disappointment.

title: Id recommend it to anyone
body: After using this app for a little under a year i can say that i would recommend this app to any gym-goer with confidence. Very useful for tracking your workouts and creating workout plans. I dont think ive been disappointed with the app a single time since i got it

title: Been using it since the beginning
body: I love being able to track supersets and it updates the workouts to the health app.

title: Great app, comprehensive list of exercising
body: I am loving this app so far, but it would be nice if there was a way to rearrange the exercises in a template.

title: Try a different app
body:
I have been using this app for a few years. It’s been great for tracking my workouts and progression. 

Unfortunately since the last few updates where it’s run from the watch instead of the phone it’s become unreliable to use. 

- Rest timers not working consistently. 
- Various sync issues such as after completing a set, it unchecks it randomly. Entire workouts go missing sometimes. Live sync works 50% of the time having to force close the phone and watch app. If I want to adjust my workout while I am in the middle of it, it is super buggy and annoying to update my plan for that workout based on how I feel that day. 
- Templates don’t always save

I hope it gets fixed once and for all since I just paid for another year of subscription. Really disappointed. Try a different app for now, honestly.

title: Templets
body: You should let people do more then three templets without the pro I know your trying to make money but like four not three you guys are just trying to take money from people

title: Great, but it freezes A LOT
body:
Love the app, love the features. One huge problem though- it freezes A LOT. During a rest interval, when the timer goes off and I go start my next set, I reopen the app and it’s usually unresponsive. I have to close the app and restart it each time. 

I also don’t think that $100 for lifetime access to all the features is a good value. Would happily pay $40-$50 especially with its current issues. 

Next set is up! Let’s see how it goes…

title: Excellent Tracker
body: Easy, interactive, and it has a great selection of exercises for the gym and home. I’ve been recommending this app to all my gym folk.

title: Constant Apple Watch Sync Issues
body: I’ve had several workouts that just aren’t saved because the Apple Watch app is horrible. Using this app with the Apple Watch is incredibly frustrating, and has been for years.

title: More then worth the money
body: Strong is a great app that I love to use tracking weight workouts.  I use many if the templates and it’s great helping me track and improve my performance.

title: Disappointed, buggy
body:
Subscribed to PRO for multiple years. App is fairly straightforward but ultimately doesn’t offer much. Essentially it allows you to build workouts into templates using their library of exercises (templates are limited to 3 unless you sign up for PRO). 

Past that, it tallies metrics (how much you’ve completed of your workout, what that ends up being in pounds, running tally of total workouts). Syncs with Apple Watch with varying degrees of success. 

Ultimately cancelled membership and deleted app for two reasons:

-There are better apps that offer better data tracking and customization for free. Ultimately the limitations of Strong and its ability to show what it’s actually done with your data are what got me to quit it. Don’t even bother with Strong PRO

-For what little it did track (in this case, workout tallies), the app inexplicably stopped syncing (and this is from someone who only uses their phone). I lost 6 months of data without any reason, and it’s not recoverable

title: Fix the syncing issues
body: I have been using this app since 2018 and I love the features but recently syncing my phone to my watch is a nightmare. Every workout I waste 15-20 minutes at the gym trying to get my watch to the home page.  I’ve restarted my watch and reinstalled the app on the daily. Please fix this

title: Intuitive and easy to use
body: I have found this app to be thr most user friendly and intuitive app for tracking weightlifting and workouts. You get 3 templates in the free version. I’ve been rotating workouts each quarter so I’ve upgraded to paid version. I’m seeing good progress now and this app really helps me stay on track, makes it easy to log and see progress, and lets me know which workout is up next by showing how many days since I did a template. Great experience overall.

title: Good app with strong potential through continued updates
body:
This is a solid app for tracking workouts, especially in its current state. It’s clean, easy to use, and does a good job of helping you stay consistent with your training. I also like the Apple Watch integration—it makes it convenient to track workouts in real time.

That said, there are a few areas where I think the app could take a big step forward. Integrating with other fitness platforms like Strava and similar apps would add a lot of value, especially for users who track multiple aspects of their training. Expanding and regularly updating the exercise library would also help streamline programming and progression over time.

One feature I’d really like to see improved is tracking for unilateral exercises (single-arm or single-leg movements). Right now, you have to manually work around this, but having built-in options to track each side individually would make the data much more accurate and useful.

There are also a few minor issues when using the Apple Watch, particularly when updating weights and reps—it can feel a bit clunky at times. Nothing major, but definitely worth refining.

Overall, it’s a good app with a strong foundation. I’ve already invested in the premium version, and I’m looking forward to seeing continued updates and improvements.

title: Great app, needs fuzzy search
body:
Love this app, I've been using it consistently and it's become a core part of my workout routine. Really well designed overall.

One thing I noticed: the exercise search doesn't handle slight typos well. For example, when I typed "flys" instead of "fly", nothing came up at all. A little fuzzy search tolerance would go a long way here. Or even Lemmatization algorithm.

Hope this helps the team! iPhone 14 Pro Max, iOS 26.3.1.

title: A Former Great
body:
I used Strong for years and it was a great app. Unfortunately the devs haven’t kept up with the times and recent sync issues with my Apple Watch have caused me to switch to a different app.

Will it do the basics and do it well? Yeah. Are there much better, more feature rich workout apps? Also, yeah.

title: Was a great app/ now doesn’t work
body: I have done over 1000 workouts on Strong and now watch and phone will not work together. All software is updated. Rebooted both multiple times. It has been a couple weeks and I’m about to go find a new app.

title: Needs Live Activity in Dynamic Island
body:
Update: uninstalled and went with Hevy. Shame because I bought a lifetime subscription so I’m throwing money out the window but this is such a critical feature. Over a year and they never built Dynamic Island and lock screen access. This is a huge miss. 

———-

The app is generally quite good. The problem is it doesn’t have Live Activity (it doesn’t show up on the Lock Screen or up at the top of the screen in the background during your workout). That means if you’re doing something else with your phone there’s no easy way to get back to your workout. You need to find the app manually again which is a big hassle if you read or whatever between sets. 

I contacted the developer back in May and they said they were working on it, but haven’t heard anything since then. I’m downgrading to three stars until then.

title: Not anymore
body: I’ve used this app for quite a while and I’m just done with it. The syncing issues with the Apple Watch are very frustrating. Often times I find the live sync will not pop up in the main app. Or things will not sync between the main app and my Apple Watch. It’s lost lost data numerous times. And after probably 10 years, I’m switching to another app.

title: Regret.
body:
This is one of those apps that I genuinely regret spending money on and waiting for them to improve or add features from their roadmap, that still haven’t appeared years later.

I just launched the Apple Watch app, now I have to sign in on the Apple Watch app as if it’s some completely disconnected thing from my phone, I use a password manager and my password is about 16 digits long, common letters, capital letters, numbers, and special characters, that I have to type manually on the tiny Apple Watch screen.

Even when using iOS keyboard to type, I can’t copy and paste the password.

I mean, who the hell designed an app where you have to enter a password and a username on a 40 millimeter screen.

The app is supposed to be a companion app, it’s like every other fitness company can get this figured out, but these guys.

title: Needs Garmin Access
body: I love the app but I love my watch more. I will be changing to a different one until they decide to unlock garmin capabilities

title: Great but..
body: Simple. Clean. Great. Would highly recommend allowing option to add “reps” or “lbs” or “time” to ANY exercise: for instance for planking I can have “time” but doesn’t allow adding “lbs” I have on my back or weighted vest, or for Frenchies I can do “reps”, but can’t have load nor duration hold to add. Also allow RPE on “timed” exercises.  Great app otherwise!

title: Best Workout app
body: This is by far the best workout app, I’ve ever try.
